extracted.intended_audience: medical product developers/manufacturers, industry consultants, and other parties applying for Medicare IPPS new technology add-on payments (and hospitals/stakeholders interested in payment policy)
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and evaluative criteria for CMS review of applications seeking Medicare IPPS new medical service or technology add-on payments, including eligibility (newness, cost, substantial clinical improvement), alternative pathways, application documentation, and public input procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newness / Substantial Similarity Criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether a technology is “new” for purposes of new technology add-on payments, including whether it is “substantially similar” to another medical product that was market authorized by FDA and has been on the market for more than 2 to 3 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS evaluates substantial similarity using three factors: (1) whether a product uses the same or a similar mechanism of action to achieve a therapeutic outcome; (2) whether a product is assigned to the same or a different MS-DRG; and (3) whether the new use of the technology involves the treatment of the same or similar type of disease and the same or similar patient population. If a technology meets all three of these criteria, it would be considered substantially similar to an existing technology and would not be considered “new.” For additional discussion, see FY 2006 and FY 2010 IPPS final rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost Criterion (high-cost threshold)
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible for the add-on payment the MS-DRG prospective payment rate otherwise applicable to discharges involving the new medical service or technology must be assessed for adequacy using a statutory formula and threshold test.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS evaluates whether charges for cases involving the new service/technology will exceed a threshold amount that is the lesser of: (a) 75 percent of the standardized amount (increased to reflect the difference between cost and charges), or (b) 75 percent of one standard deviation beyond the geometric mean standardized charge for all cases in the MS-DRG to which the technology is assigned (or the case-weighted average of all relevant MS-DRGs if the technology occurs in many MS-DRGs). Applicants should submit a significant sample of data of sufficient size to enable initial validation and analysis. Beginning FY2022 CMS uses proposed threshold values associated with the proposed rule to evaluate the cost criterion; proposed thresholds for future years are published in associated data files on CMS.gov. See also HIPAA Privacy Rule considerations for claims information submitted with applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantial Clinical Improvement Criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: A medical service or technology must represent an advance that substantially improves, relative to technologies previously available, the diagnosis or treatment of Medicare beneficiaries (the totality of the circumstances is considered).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A determination that the technology substantially improves diagnosis or treatment means one or more of: the technology offers a treatment option for a patient population unresponsive to or ineligible for current treatments; offers the ability to diagnose a condition that is currently undetectable or earlier diagnosis with evidence that diagnosis affects patient management; or significantly improves clinical outcomes as demonstrated by reduction in clinically significant adverse events (including mortality), decreased rate of subsequent diagnostic or therapeutic interventions, decreased future hospitalizations or physician visits, faster resolution/reduced length of stay, improved activities of daily living, improved quality of life, or greater medication adherence/compliance. The totality of circumstances may otherwise demonstrate substantial improvement. Evidence acceptable may include clinical trials, peer-reviewed articles, study results, meta-analyses, consensus statements, white papers, patient surveys, case studies, systematic reviews, letters from major healthcare associations, editorials, and public comments. The medical condition may have low prevalence or the improvement may apply to a subpopulation. CMS does not rely on FDA safety/effectiveness standards to determine substantial clinical improvement for Medicare purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative Pathway — Breakthrough Devices Program (transformative devices)
rubrics_metrics.description: A medical device designated under FDA's Breakthrough Devices Program that has received FDA marketing authorization may be considered not substantially similar to an existing technology and need not meet the substantial clinical improvement requirement under §412.87(b)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under this alternative pathway the device must have received Breakthrough designation and FDA marketing authorization (approved, cleared, or De Novo granted) for the indication covered by the designation and must meet all other requirements in §412.87(c). CMS reviews the application based only on the alternative pathway specified by the applicant at time of submission. Note: CMS proposed to repeal the alternative pathway beginning with FY2028 applications in a later section; applicants should monitor rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative Pathway — Certain Antimicrobial Products (QIDP and LPAD)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain antimicrobial products designated by FDA as Qualified Infectious Disease Products (QIDP) or approved under the Limited Population Pathway for Antibacterial and Antifungal Drugs (LPAD) may qualify under an alternative pathway and be considered not substantially similar to an existing technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a QIDP or LPAD product received FDA marketing authorization (and, beginning FY2022, LPAD approval used for the approved indication), it will not need to meet the substantial clinical improvement requirement and must meet the requirements of §412.87(d). CMS finalized policy clarifications that the product must receive FDA marketing authorization for the indication covered by the designation/approval. For certain antimicrobial products CMS also finalized conditional approval policies allowing earlier receipt of add-on payments in some circumstances (subject to timing and documentation rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Add-on Payment Amounts and Limits (payment mechanism)
rubrics_metrics.description: The add-on payment is based on hospital cost for the new medical service or technology; capital costs are excluded and the payment is limited in specified ways.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For discharges before Oct 1, 2019, the add-on equaled the lesser of (1) 50% of the costs of the new service/technology or (2) 50% of the amount by which case costs exceed the standard DRG payment. Beginning Oct 1, 2019, for technologies other than QIDPs, the add-on equals the lesser of (1) 65% of the costs of the new service/technology or (2) 65% of the amount by which case costs exceed the standard DRG payment. For QIDPs (and LPAD-approved products beginning Oct 1, 2020) the add-on is the lesser of 75% of costs or 75% of the amount costs exceed the DRG payment. For certain gene therapies indicated and used specifically for sickle cell disease (FY2025 decisions), CMS finalized a 75% add-on during the 2–3-year newness period. Unless the discharge qualifies for an outlier payment, additional Medicare payment is limited to the full MS-DRG payment plus 65% (or 75% for certain antimicrobial products) of the estimated costs of the new technology. CMS does not include capital-related costs in add-on payments. Section 503(d)(2) of MMA provides no budget neutrality reduction due to add-on payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation Sequence and FDA marketing authorization timing
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS first determines whether a technology meets the newness criterion and only if so then assesses the cost threshold and whether it represents a substantial clinical improvement. Applicants must have FDA marketing authorization by certain deadlines to be eligible for the upcoming fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historically applicants had to have FDA approval/clearance by July 1 prior to the fiscal year; beginning with FY2025 applications CMS finalized requiring FDA marketing authorization by May 1 prior to the fiscal year (except for applications under certain alternative pathways, subject to change if CMS repeals alternative pathways). For technologies not already FDA market authorized for the application indication (beginning FY2025), applicants must have a complete and active FDA market authorization request at time of application and must provide documentation of FDA acceptance (for 510(k)/De Novo) or filing (for PMA/NDA/BLA). For FY2027 applicants resubmitting after a CRL must provide FDA resubmission acknowledgement letter indicating the new FDA goal date. CMS recognizes different FDA processes (e.g., eSTAR) and accepts appropriate documentation (e.g., eSTAR review assignment notification).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Content Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: What applicants must submit to CMS when seeking new technology add-on payments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must submit a formal request including a full description of the clinical applications of the medical service or technology and the results of any clinical evaluations demonstrating that the technology represents a substantial clinical improvement (unless under an applicable alternative pathway), along with a significant sample of data to demonstrate the technology meets the high-cost threshold. Complete application information and final deadlines will be posted on the CMS website. Beginning with certain application cycles CMS will also post the applicant's explanation of cost analysis methodology and step-by-step columns used in the cost analysis spreadsheet (with some cost/charge values excluded from public posting).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Posting and Confidentiality Rules for Applications
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS policy to publicly post new technology add-on payment applications and what materials will be excluded as confidential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beginning with the FY2024 application cycle CMS will publicly post applications (except withdrawn pre-publication). With the exception of information included in a confidential information section, cost and volume information, and materials identified by applicant as copyrighted or not otherwise releasable, contents of the application and related materials may be posted. The cost analysis spreadsheet attachment and other cost or charge values provided in cost criterion responses are not included in the public posting, though cost and volume information may be summarized and discussed in the proposed rule. Applicants should identify confidential material where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Input Process Prior to Proposed Rulemaking
rubrics_metrics.description: Statutory and procedural obligations to provide for public input regarding whether a medical service or technology represents a substantial clinical improvement before publication of a proposed rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 1886(d)(5)(K)(viii) requires the Secretary to: provide for public input before the proposed rule, make public and update a list of services/technologies with pending add-on applications, accept comments/recommendations/data from the public, and provide a meeting at which organizations representing hospitals, physicians, manufacturers and interested parties may present comments/recommendations/data to CMS clinical staff. CMS has implemented town hall meetings (virtual) and considers presentations and written comments received by specified deadlines for evaluations limited to the substantial clinical improvement criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and Privacy / HIPAA considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on submission of claims/charge data and applicability of HIPAA Privacy Rule to claims information submitted with applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS discussed in prior rulemaking (Sept 7, 2001 and FY2012 final rule) whether HIPAA Privacy Rule at 45 CFR part 160 and subparts A and E of 45 CFR part 164 applies to claims information providers submit with applications. Applicants should consult FY2012 IPPS/LTCH PPS final rule for details. Applicants must submit sufficient data samples for validation; CMS notes data collection burden is subject to PRA and OMB control number 0938-1347.

rubrics_metrics.name: ICD-10-PCS Section “X” Codes Handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for coding certain new medical services and technologies within ICD-10-PCS Section “X” codes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions to create, delete, or revise Section “X” codes will be referred to the ICD-10 Coordination and Maintenance Committee. Several new services/technologies approved for add-on payments may be assigned a Section “X” code; CMS has posted ICD-10-PCS Guidelines (including Section “X” codes) on CMS.gov and encourages providers to review them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pharmaceutical & Technology Ombudsman (PTO) assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS provides a centralized Ombudsman to assist interested parties navigating innovation pathways including new technology add-on payments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PTO can point interested parties to process/requirements/timelines, coordinate engagement with CMS components, serve as a primary contact and provide updates where appropriate. CMS posts resources and a guide for medical technology companies and other interested parties on its website; parties may contact PharmTechOmbud@cms.hhs.gov for further discussion.
